t: To carry out parts B and G of title VII and part A of title VIII of the Act, $203,000,000, of which $175,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, teaching facilities pursuant to section 720 of the Act including $35,000,000 for dental facilities as authorized by subsections (2) and (3) of said section, $10,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, facilities for collegiate schools of nursing; $15,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, facilities for associate degree and diploma schools of nursing; and $3,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, facilities for training centers for allied health professions: Provided, That amounts appropriated herein shall remain available until expended.

fable.w: This section only appropriates funds for construction grants to health professions and nursing schools and says the money remains available until expended. The tempting reading is that grants to outside institutions bring them into a federal process, but receiving or applying for grants is expressly excluded from participation. Nothing here requires consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: $175,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, teaching facilities pursuant to section 720 of the Act

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes funding for grants. It does not describe any process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants from being considered participation.
qwen_block.s: $203,000,000, of which $175,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, teaching facilities pursuant to section 720 of the Act

opus.w: This section only sets aside money for construction grants and says the money stays available until spent. Outside institutions may receive the grants, but grant applications and awards are expressly excluded from participation. Nothing here requires a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: $175,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, teaching facilities pursuant to section 720 of the Act

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations for grants to outside entities (schools and training centers). The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or input from these outside entities before the federal government makes the decision to appropriate or distribute the funds; they are merely recipients of financial assistance.
qwen_chat.s: To carry out parts B and G of title VII and part A of title VIII of the Act, $203,000,000, of which $175,000,000 is for grants to assist in construction of new, or replacement or rehabilitation of existing, teaching facilities pursuant to section 720 of the Act
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the grants are given to schools and training centers (outside entities), this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." The section describes the appropriation of funds for grants, not a process of consultation or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. The recipients are beneficiaries, not participants in the decision-making process.
